text:
jia: Customer in EU reporting intermittent 502s and TLS resets when we autoscale edge nodes. They have an on-prem outbound proxy + strict allowlist. Any ideas?

 tom: do we have the exact egress IPs they whitelisted? sounds like SNAT rotation or IP churn when we add nodes. Can you paste the client logs?

 maria: they pasted some snippets — 'tls: handshake failure' and 'CONNECT https://callback.example.com:443 403 Forbidden' for requests coming from a subset of our IPs. Other IPs succeed.

 sam: classic case of their proxy/firewall only accepting a tight set of source IPs. When our autoscaler adds capacity the source IP changes and their proxy drops it. Could also be port exhaustion on their proxy causing weird resets.

 jia: customer says policy only allows IP-based allowlists (no FQDN). They want a small, stable set of /24s that "won't change". We currently publish a daily manifest of egress prefixes which they don't accept.

 tom: short-term: offer them a pinned egress pool. We already have a dedicated egress feature for Dedicated customers — can we carve a tiny dedicated pool for Hosted? If not, customer-tunnel/private-link is another option.

 maria: for immediate mitigation we can also ask their proxy team to allow HTTP CONNECT to our domains and permit SNI passthrough (avoid TLS MITM). If their proxy inspects certs, it needs to trust our certs or it'll break handshake.

 sam: network tips to give the customer: 1) whitelist the region prefix list (we can provide the region CIDRs); 2) ensure proxy's SNAT port pool is large (avoid < 10000 ephemeral ports) to prevent port reuse; 3) allow CONNECT on 443 for our hostnames.

 kevin (support): I'll send the signed IP manifest + a small doc with recommended NAT port ranges and example proxy rules. Quick checklist I'm going to share:
  - whitelist region CIDRs we supply
  - enable CONNECT to callback hostnames and allow SNI passthrough
  - increase proxy SNAT ephemeral port range (e.g. 32768-61000)
  - confirm proxy logs for 403/handshake timestamps we requested

 jia: long-term proposal: product add-on to expose 'Pinned Egress' (static source IPs for hosted customers) + provisioning flag to prefer nodes from same NAT pool so churn is minimized. I'll open RDW-5423 for tracking.

 infra-bot: Incident created RDW-5423: "Pinned egress IP pool for hosted customers" — assignee: eng-platform, priority: P2

 tom: action item for docs: add a troubleshooting checklist for customer-facing eng/support with exact captures to request (tcpdump, proxy logs, source IP seen, client timestamp window, example curl).

 maria: I'll draft the KB entry and include sample commands: 
```
# capture example curl to reproduce via proxy
curl -v --proxy http://corp-proxy:3128 https://callback.example.com/health
```

 sam: also recommend advising customers not to create stateful rules based on ephemeral source ports — use FQDNs where possible. If they insist on IPs, use our pinned pool or region prefixes and accept daily updates. :thumbsup: 

 jia: thanks all — I'll coordinate with the customer, send the manifest, and follow up on RDW-5423.
